It has been previously shown that -crossing-critical graphs have bounded path-width and contain only a bounded number of internally disjoint paths between any two vertices. We expand on these results, providing a more detailed description of the structure of crossing-critical graphs. On the way towards this description, we prove a new structural result on plane graphs of bounded path-width. Consequently, a great deal of research work has been invested into understanding what forces the graph crossing number to be high. There exist strong quantitative lower bounds, such as the famous Crossing Lemma [1, 19].
